aiOverview.content: The NCAA Division I Men’s Basketball Tournament (March Madness) has crowned a champion annually since 1939, with a notable exception in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. UCLA holds the record for most titles (11), primarily under coach John Wooden, while recent champions include UConn (2023, 2024), Kansas (2022), and Baylor (2021). Recent NCAA Men's Basketball Champions 2026: TBD (Tournament underway) 2025: TBD 2024: UConn (Defeated Purdue) 2023: UConn (Defeated San Diego State) 2022: Kansas (Defeated North Carolina) 2021: Baylor (Defeated Gonzaga) 2020: Canceled 2019: Virginia (Defeated Texas Tech) 2018: Villanova (Defeated Michigan) 2017: North Carolina (Defeated Gonzaga) 2016: Villanova (Defeated North Carolina) 2015: Duke (Defeated Wisconsin) Historical Highlights Most Titles: UCLA (11) Most Consecutive Titles: UCLA (7 from 1967–1973) First Champion: Oregon (1939) Detailed Winners (1939–2024) 2010s: UConn ('11, '14), Duke ('10, '15), Kentucky ('12), Louisville ('13), Villanova ('16, '18), North Carolina ('17), Virginia ('19) 2000s: Florida ('06, '07), North Carolina ('05, '09), UConn ('04), Syracuse ('03), Maryland ('02), Duke ('01), Michigan State ('00), Kansas ('08) 1990s: Kentucky ('96, '98), Duke ('91, '92), UCLA ('95), Arkansas ('94), North Carolina ('93), Arizona ('97), UConn ('99) 1980s: Indiana ('81, '87), Louisville ('80, '86), North Carolina ('82), NC State ('83), Georgetown ('84), Villanova ('85), Michigan ('89), Kansas ('88) (List continues back to 1939, dominated by UCLA in the 60s/70s).
